newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks give ground despite improved inflation.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks give ground despite improved inflation.

text.p: Greek shares traded weak throughout the session with the benchmark share index settling 0.33 percent lower with trading volume dropping to 4.9 billion drachmas despite an improved October inflation figure.
October inflation slowed to 8.3 percent year-on-year from 8.5 percent in September, the National Statistics Service said on Wednesday.
The CPI came out slightly below market expectations as economists polled by Reuters produced a mean forecast of 8.4 percent year-on-year.

"The market is subdued with demand on the weak side. The recent law on investment services has dampened liquidity as short sellers and quasi margin traders are being phased out. This is evidenced by the drop in volume," said broker Nick Kapatos at Olympic Securities.
"I see more of the same despite some good news out there. Quality stocks and blue chips are holding the benchmark index right now," he said.

Financial market focus has turned to government plans to tax interest earned on T-bills, derivatives such as swaps, options and FRAs and revamp the tax status of mutual funds as the market awaits the 1997 budget.
The IFC Corporation revised its IFCI Greece share index, adding five new shares -- Alte Technical, OTE telecom OTEr.AT, Parnassos, Aspis and Alpha Finance.
It said the Athens bourse had a low correlation with other world equity markets and was good for portfolio diversification.
And the European Commission forecast on Wednesday that Greece along with Italy and Britain would not meet the Maastricht Treaty's budget deficit criteria in 1997.
